examples.en: After work I had a glass of soju with a friend.
How about a glass of soju after so long?
I introduced soju to my foreign friend.

examples.ko: 한국 식당에서 소주는 보통 작은 잔에 따라 마셔요.
examples.en: In Korean restaurants, soju is usually poured into small glasses.
The soju glass is small, so it empties quickly.

examples.ko: 삼겹살을 먹을 때 소주 생각이 난다고 아버지가 말했어요.
examples.en: My father said he thinks of soju when he eats pork belly.

explain: 한국을 대표하는 술 중 하나로 보통 '한 잔', '한 병'으로 세요. 맥주와 섞은 것은 '소맥'이라고 해요. 어른과 함께 마실 때는 술을 두 손으로 받는 예절이 있어요.

phrases.en: I drank a bottle of soju with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소주를 세는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: How to count soju.

phrases.en: I drink soju with my family on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 술을 마신다고 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for drinking alcohol.

phrases.en: I drank soju mixed with beer with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소주와 맥주를 섞은 술이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drink made by mixing soju and beer.

explain_en: It is one of Korea's best-known drinks and is counted as '한 잔' (a glass) or '한 병' (a bottle). Soju mixed with beer is called '소맥'. When drinking with elders, there is an etiquette of receiving the drink with both hands.

examples.en: I add a little vinegar to cold noodles.
I wipe the window with vinegar.
I bought a bottle of vinegar.
The vinegar is too sour.
I sprinkle olive oil and vinegar on the salad.
The vinegar smell was strong, so I opened the window.

explain: 맛은 '시다'로 말해요. 줄여서 '초'라고도 하고 '초고추장'은 고추장에 식초를 넣은 소스예요. 요리뿐 아니라 청소에도 쓰는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: I put vinegar in the salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when cooking.

phrases.en: I eat naengmyeon with a little vinegar added.
phrases.nuance_ko: '식초'를 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 'sikcho', used casually in speech.

phrases.en: Please add one spoonful of vinegar to the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양을 말할 때 '한 숟가락'처럼 단위를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a unit like 'han sutgarak' to say the amount.

explain_en: Its taste is described with '시다' (sour). It is sometimes shortened to '초', and '초고추장' is red pepper paste mixed with vinegar. Many people use it for cleaning as well as cooking.

examples.en: I bought 20 kilograms of rice.
I wash the rice to cook it.
We've run out of rice, so I have to go to the supermarket.
The price of rice went up a lot this year.
I make rice cakes from rice.
This rice is delicious.

explain: 익히기 전은 '쌀', 익힌 것은 '밥', 논에서 자라는 식물은 '벼'예요. 쌀은 '씻다', '떨어지다'와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I wash the rice before cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 지을 때 먼저 하는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first step before cooking rice.

phrases.en: We've run out of rice, so I'm going to buy some.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀이 다 없어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the rice has run out.

phrases.en: Today I ate white rice with kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀로만 지은 밥을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cooked rice made only from rice.

explain_en: Before cooking it is '쌀', cooked it is '밥', and the plant growing in the paddy is '벼'. '쌀' often goes with '씻다' (wash) and '떨어지다' (run out).

examples.en: I went to bed late last night.
My husband is coming home late today.
Yesterday's meeting ended late.
I got up late this morning. I was very busy.
I came late. I'm sorry.

explain: 반대말은 “일찍”이에요. 일찍 자요 ↔ 늦게 자요. “빨리”의 반대말은 “천천히”예요.

phrases.ko: 늦게 배운 도둑이 날 새는 줄 모른다
phrases.example: 늦게 배운 도둑이 날 새는 줄 모른다더니 요즘 게임에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: someone who starts something late gets more absorbed in it
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦게 시작해서 더 빠질 때
phrases.nuance_en: used about someone who starts late but gets even more absorbed than others
phrases.en_equiv: someone who starts something late gets more absorbed in it

explain_en: The opposite is 일찍: 일찍 자요 (go to bed early) ↔ 늦게 자요. The opposite of 빨리 is 천천히.

examples.en: I'll keep studying Korean from now on too.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와도 선수들은 경기를 계속했어요.
examples.en: The players continued the game even in heavy rain.
That's interesting, please go on with the story.
I want to keep working at this company.
I'll keep exercising even if my legs hurt.

examples.ko: 피곤한데 계속하면 병이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep going while tired, you could get sick.

explain: 하던 일을 이어서 한다는 쓰임인데, 말할 때는 '계속 공부해요', '계속 먹어요'처럼 '계속' 뒤에 동사를 바로 붙이는 게 더 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '그만하다'이고, 잠깐 멈출 때는 '쉬다'를 써요. '계속해 주세요'는 상대에게 하던 말이나 일을 이어 가라고 할 때 아주 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I keep studying even when it is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계속' 뒤에 동사를 바로 붙이면 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a verb right after 계속 sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Good. Please continue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방에게 하던 일을 이어서 해 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to go on with what they were doing.

phrases.en: I want to continue this work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여서 이어서 하고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 싶다 expresses the wish to carry on.

explain_en: Transitive; you keep doing an action, needs an object. In everyday speech people more often put '계속' before another verb, as in '계속 공부해요' (I keep studying), than use '계속하다' itself. The opposite is '그만하다' (stop doing); for a short break use '쉬다'. '계속해 주세요' is a very common way to tell someone to go on.

dis.h: keep doing something; needs an object
gh: go on without stopping; has no object
continue by linking to what came before
formal; keep existing, like an institution

p.n: 계속되다 takes no object and needs 이/가 on the subject, so the word can't just be swapped.

t90.ax: I want to keep working at this company.

en: to date; to go out with

examples.en: I go on a date with my boyfriend every weekend.

examples.ko: 어제 한강 공원에서 여자 친구와 데이트했어요.
examples.en: I went on a date with my girlfriend at the Han River park yesterday.
Who are you dating these days?
I'm going on my first date this evening.
I bought flowers on the way to the date.
I happened to see my friend out on a date.

explain: '데이트하다'는 연인이나 서로 마음이 있는 사이에서만 써요. 그냥 친구와 만나는 건 '만나다', '놀다'라고 해요. 소개를 받아 처음 만나는 자리는 '소개팅'이라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.example: 오늘 저녁에 여자 친구와 데이트를 해요.
phrases.en: I have a date with my girlfriend this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '데이트하다'를 '데이트 + 를 하다'로 나눠 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb split into 'date + 를 하다'.

phrases.en: I have a date planned for tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연인과 만나기로 한 약속을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a plan to meet a partner.

phrases.example: 주말에 남자 친구와 영화관에 데이트하러 가요.
phrases.en: On the weekend I go to the movie theater on a date with my boyfriend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 데이트를 하려고 어디로 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means going somewhere in order to have a date.

explain_en: A single outing together; everyday. 데이트하다 is only for couples or people who are romantically interested in each other. Meeting a plain friend is '만나다' or '놀다'. A first meeting arranged through an introduction has its own word, '소개팅' (blind date).

dis.h: go out on a date together

p.n: The relationship verb does not fit a single outing.

t90.ax: Who are you dating these days?

examples.en: There was leftover kimchi in the fridge, so I made kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥에 계란 프라이를 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is tasty with a fried egg on top.
For lunch I want to eat kimchi fried rice.

examples.ko: 김치볶음밥은 만들기 쉬워서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Kimchi fried rice is easy to make, so I cook it often.

examples.ko: 친구가 만든 김치볶음밥 맛이 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: The kimchi fried rice my friend made tasted really good.

examples.ko: 여기요, 김치볶음밥 하나랑 라면 하나 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one kimchi fried rice and one ramyeon, please.

explain: 김치를 넣고 볶은 밥이에요. 집에서는 '만들다'나 '해 먹다'를 쓰고, 식당에서는 '시키다'나 '주문하다'를 써요. 새우볶음밥, 야채볶음밥처럼 앞에 재료를 붙여 다른 볶음밥도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I ordered kimchi fried rice at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 음식을 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering food at a restaurant.

phrases.en: I made kimchi fried rice for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 만들어 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make and eat it yourself at home.
phrases.en_equiv: to make and eat kimchi fried rice

phrases.en: One bowl of kimchi fried rice, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 양을 말하며 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the amount when ordering at a restaurant.
phrases.en_equiv: a bowl of kimchi fried rice

explain_en: It is fried rice stir-fried with kimchi. At home people say '만들다' or '해 먹다', and at a restaurant '시키다' or '주문하다'. You can put other ingredients in front, as in 새우볶음밥 or 야채볶음밥, to name other fried rice dishes.

examples.en: I eat lunch at a restaurant near my office.
What did you eat for lunch today?

examples.ko: 동생이 점심밥을 먹고 바로 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling ate lunch and went straight to school.

examples.ko: 점심밥 먹을 시간도 없을 만큼 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was so busy I didn't even have time for lunch.
I brought gimbap for lunch.

examples.ko: 학교 점심밥이 맛있어서 한 그릇 더 먹었어요.
examples.en: The school lunch was tasty, so I had another bowl.

explain: 보통은 그냥 '점심'이라고 하고, '점심밥'은 밥 먹는 것을 조금 더 구체적으로 말하는 편한 표현이에요. 격식 있게는 '점심 식사'라고 해요. 싸 가지고 가는 점심은 '도시락'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Did you eat lunch?
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥'을 빼고 더 짧고 자연스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and more natural without '밥'.

phrases.en: Lunch is at twelve o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking more formally.

phrases.en: I brought a packed lunch today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 싸 가지고 가는 점심을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lunch you pack at home and carry with you.

explain_en: People usually just say '점심', and '점심밥' is a casual way to talk about the meal more concretely. The formal version is '점심 식사'. A packed lunch you carry along is called '도시락'.
